item.description: 3365#Re-consider publishing to the npm registry#
item.content:encoded:
npm 12 has changed some defaults to harden security, including shipping with allow-remote=none by default.

If the package is a direct dependency of my project, I have to explicitly set allow-remote=root.

However, if a dependency uses xlsx, I'd have to set allow-remote=all. I believe this actively hurts consumers of this package, as usage now requires disabling security features.

I hope publishing to npm registry in addition could be considered.

item.title: jonathanelmgren opened issue sheetjs/sheetjs#3360
item.description: 3360#.xlsb shared formulas decode to impossible references (column wraps to `XF*`, row wraps to ~1048714)#
item.content:encoded:
Summary

When reading a binary .xlsb workbook, SheetJS decodes shared formulas
with incorrect relative offsets. Once a shared formula's relative reference has
a sufficiently negative offset, the decoded column wraps toward the XF*
band (near max column 16384) and the row wraps past the max row 1,048,576
(e.g. to 1048577).

A reference to row 1048577 is impossible (Excel's max row is 1,048,576), so
the parser is emitting garbage. The cached value of each affected cell
decodes correctly, and the same workbook saved as .xlsx parses correctly,
which isolates the defect to SheetJS's .xlsb shared-formula reference
decoding. Excel and LibreOffice open the .xlsb with correct formulas.

Minimal reproduction

https://github.com/jonathanelmgren/sheetjs-xlsb-shared-formula-bug

git clone https://github.com/jonathanelmgren/sheetjs-xlsb-shared-formula-bug
cd sheetjs-xlsb-shared-formula-bug
pnpm install   # or: npm install
pnpm start     # or: node repro.js

The repo bundles the same one-sheet workbook in both formats
(shared-formula-fixture.xlsx authored programmatically, then re-saved by Excel
as shared-formula-fixture.xlsb). The script reads both and prints the
contrast.

Versions

Reproduced identically on:

  • xlsx@0.18.5 (npm)
  • xlsx@0.20.3 (https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/xlsx-0.20.3.tgz)

Node.js 22, macOS.

Steps to reproduce

const XLSX = require("xlsx");
const fs = require("fs");
const wb = XLSX.read(fs.readFileSync("shared-formula-fixture.xlsb"), {
  type: "buffer",
  cellFormula: true,
});
const ws = wb.Sheets["repro"];
for (const cell of ["L5", "M5", "N5", "O5"]) {
  console.log(cell, ws[cell] && ws[cell].f);
}

The fixture sheet repro contains shared formulas with negative-offset
relative references: a 12-wide trailing window on row 5
(=SUM(<c-11>1:<c>1)/SUM(<c-11>3:<c>3)) and a vertical 2-row sum on row 10
(=SUM(<c>8:<c>9)).

Expected (and what reading the .xlsx returns)

L5 =SUM(A1:L1)/SUM(A3:L3)
M5 =SUM(B1:M1)/SUM(B3:M3)
N5 =SUM(C1:N1)/SUM(C3:N3)
O5 =SUM(D1:O1)/SUM(D3:O3)

Actual (reading the .xlsb)

L5 =SUM(XFE1048577:L1048577)/SUM(XFE1048579:L1048579)   <- CORRUPT
M5 =SUM(XFF1048577:M1048577)/SUM(XFF1048579:M1048579)   <- CORRUPT
N5 =SUM(XFG1048577:N1048577)/SUM(XFG1048579:N1048579)   <- CORRUPT
O5 =SUM(XFH1048577:O1048577)/SUM(XFH1048579:O1048579)   <- CORRUPT

The column wraps (A -> XFE) and the row wraps (1 -> 1048577). All 69
formula cells in the fixture are affected. In a larger real-world workbook we
saw ~15% of all formula cells corrupted this way.

Impact

The cached values are intact, so read-only value extraction is unaffected. But
any consumer that recalculates formulas (re-evaluating in a formula engine,
or re-saving a recalculated workbook) gets wrong results or #DIV/0!, because
the corrupt ranges point at empty far-corner cells.

item.description: 3355#URL-pinned transitive xlsx dependency breaks pnpm v11 hardened installs#
item.content:encoded:
First of all thanks for maintaining SheetJS.

We ran into a dependency resolution issue in a pnpm v11 workspace with hardened supply-chain settings enabled.

xlsx is currently pulled as a transitive dependency via a URL/exotic source in one of our dependency chains. With blockExoticSubdeps enabled, pnpm correctly blocks this and install fails with:

ERR_PNPM_EXOTIC_SUBDEP: Exotic dependency "xlsx" (resolved via url) is not allowed in subdependencies when blockExoticSubdeps is enabled

Could you switch this path to a normal registry-published dependency (instead of URL-pinned/exotic resolution) so strict pnpm installs work without exceptions?

Thanks a lot!

item.title: mmarkell opened issue sheetjs/sheetjs#3354
item.description: 3354#`SSF.is_date` false positive on XML-tag-style numFmt formatCodes#
item.content:encoded:
Affected versions: observed on xlsx@0.20.3.

Summary

SSF.is_date(fmt) returns true for non-Excel format codes whose text body happens
to contain a lowercase date-token letter (m, d, y, h, s). Some legacy
ERP/accounting exporters emit numFmt entries like <widget><dec:2> or
<amount><dec:9> in xl/styles.xml — these are not valid Excel format codes, but
the is_date heuristic flags them as dates because of the d in "widget" / "dec",
or the m in "amount". With cellDates: true, every numeric cell using such a
format gets converted to a JS Date near the Excel epoch (1899-12-31), and the
Date then formats as 01/00/1900 (or similar) downstream.

Minimal repro

import { SSF } from "xlsx";

console.log(SSF.is_date("<amount>"));         // → true   (should be false)
console.log(SSF.is_date("<dec:9>"));          // → true   (should be false)
console.log(SSF.is_date("<amount><dec:9>"));  // → true   (should be false)
console.log(SSF.is_date("<widget><dec:2>"));  // → true   (should be false)

// Real Excel formats — must continue to return correct results
console.log(SSF.is_date("m/d/yyyy"));         // → true   (correct)
console.log(SSF.is_date("[Red]#,##0.00"));    // → false  (correct)

End-to-end repro

fixtures/bogus_numfmt_repro.xlsx is a 2.5 KB
synthetic XLSX with generic widget-inventory data (id / color / price) where the
price column references a custom numFmtId=164 whose formatCode is
<widget><dec:2>.

Reader:

import { read } from "xlsx";
import fs from "fs";

const wb = read(fs.readFileSync("./bogus_numfmt_repro.xlsx"), {
    dense: true,
    raw: true,
    cellDates: true,
});
const data = wb.Sheets.Inventory["!data"];
for (let r = 1; r < data.length; r++) {
    const c = data[r][2]; // price column
    console.log(`row ${r}: t=${c.t}, v=${c.v}`);
}

Observed output on xlsx@0.20.3:

row 1: t=d, v=1899-12-31T00:01:08.032Z   ← source value was 0.0007874
row 2: t=d, v=1900-01-01T12:00:00.000Z   ← source value was 1.50
row 3: t=d, v=1900-02-11T23:45:36.000Z   ← source value was 42.99

Expected output (with the patch below):

row 1: t=n, v=0.0007874
row 2: t=n, v=1.5
row 3: t=n, v=42.99

Root cause

fmt_is_date (xlsx.js ~line 956 in 0.20.3) tokenizes the format string and skips
literal segments — quoted strings ("…"), escaped chars (\…), bracketed segments
([…]) — but falls through default for <. After incrementing past the < it
encounters the letters of the tag body and hits the case 'a': / case 'm': /
case 'd': arms, which return true on the first date-token they see.

So is_date("<amount>") returns true because:

  1. i=0: char is <, falls to default, ++i.
  2. i=1: char is a, hits case 'a':, looks ahead for A/P / AM/PM, no match, ++i.
  3. i=2: char is m, hits case 'm': → return true.

< and > are not valid Excel format-code characters outside of bracketed
conditionals (e.g. [<100]), and bracketed conditionals are already consumed by the
existing case '[' branch before they reach case '<'. So a literal <
encountered at the top level always indicates a non-Excel custom payload.

Proposed patch

Mirror the existing '[' skip-segment handling — treat < as the start of an
opaque segment that ends at the next > (or end of string):

 function fmt_is_date(fmt) {
     var i = 0, c = "", o = "";
     while(i < fmt.length) {
         switch((c = fmt.charAt(i))) {
             case 'G': if(SSF_isgeneral(fmt, i)) i+= 6; i++; break;
             case '"': for(;(fmt.charCodeAt(++i)) !== 34 && i < fmt.length;){} ++i; break;
             case '\\': i+=2; break;
             …
             case '[':
                 o = c;
                 while(fmt.charAt(i++) !== ']' && i < fmt.length) o += fmt.charAt(i);
                 if(o.match(SSF_abstime)) return true;
                 break;
+            case '<':
+                /* Skip XML-tag-style annotations like <amount> or <dec:9> that some
+                   ERP exporters emit in xl/styles.xml. These are not valid Excel
+                   format codes — but without this branch, letters inside the tag
+                   (e.g. "m" in "amount") incorrectly fall into the date-token arms
+                   and the format is misclassified as a date. */
+                while(i < fmt.length && fmt.charAt(i++) !== '>'){/* empty */}
+                break;
             …
             default: ++i; break;
         }
     }
     return false;
 }

The patch is conservative: a top-level < is never valid Excel format syntax, and
bracketed conditionals like [<100] are unaffected because they're handled by the
existing '[' branch before this point.

Suggested tests

// Regression — XML-tag-style annotations in numFmt formatCodes
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("<amount>"),         false);
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("<dec:9>"),          false);
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("<amount><dec:9>"),  false);
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("<widget><dec:2>"),  false);
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("<unclosed"),        false); // graceful on malformed input

// Existing behaviors must still hold
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("m/d/yyyy"),         true);
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("h:mm:ss"),          true);
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("[$-409]m/d/yy"),    true);
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("[Red]#,##0.00"),    false);
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("[<100]0.00"),       false); // bracketed conditional
assert.equal(SSF.is_date("\"month\": 0.00"),  false); // letters inside quotes

item.title: k1rnt opened issue sheetjs/sheetjs#3345
item.description: 3345#Add optional link protocol validation for HTML export#
item.content:encoded:
As discussed via email, it would be helpful to have an optional opt-in flag
for sheet_to_html(), write(), and writeFile() to restrict hyperlink
protocols when exporting to HTML.

This would be particularly useful for web applications that preview
untrusted Excel files, helping reduce the risk of unsafe URL schemes
(e.g. javascript:) being included in generated HTML.

Suggested API shape (example):

XLSX.utils.sheet_to_html(worksheet, { sanitizeLinks: true });
XLSX.write(workbook, { bookType: "html", sanitizeLinks: true });

When enabled, the option could allow only:

  • http / https URLs
  • internal links (e.g. #sheet1!A1)

The default behavior would remain unchanged to preserve Excel
compatibility, while offering a safer opt-in path for web-facing use cases.
item.author: k1rnt
